caveats.ui_banner: Feasibility = technically feasible IF the assumed water allocation is supplied; water source, groundwater and wastewater availability are not mapped. All outcomes are simulated, none observed.

expert_rule: Maas-Hoffman salinity response (FAO IDP29 Table 4), ESP tolerance classes (FAO SB39), pH/SOC/coarse-fragment/texture/depth/slope response curves (assumed shapes)

simulated: intervention outcomes (leaching, gypsum, organic amendment, terracing, water harvesting)
post-restoration relative yield, class and water requirement

model1_run.confidence_method: Monte-Carlo agreement: share of 24 draws (SoilGrids/SOTWIS/terrain/climate inputs perturbed by documented error models, ML ensemble member and fusion thresholds resampled) that reproduce the central class. It measures robustness to input uncertainty, NOT validated map accuracy.

label_basis.ece: measured saturated-paste EC (WoSIS ELCOSP + Hassani 2020 points), topsoil 0-30 cm
label_basis.restoration_outcomes: NONE observed: no before/after restoration dataset exists in the sources checked; outcomes are simulated from documented relationships
label_basis.feasibility_classes: Monte-Carlo success probability cut at expert-rule thresholds (0.15/0.40/0.70)

irr_fresh.name: Drip irrigation with fresh groundwater + reclamation leaching, gypsum and organic amendment

irr_tww.name: Treated-wastewater drip irrigation, salt-tolerant crops, leaching and gypsum

irr_brackish.name: Brackish-groundwater drip irrigation with salt-tolerant crops (biosaline agriculture)

rainfed_wh.name: Rain-fed cultivation with microcatchment water harvesting and mulch/organic amendment

terraced_irr.name: Bench terraces with soil conservation and drip irrigation (sloping land)

factor_assumptions.RY_sodicity: piecewise-linear: 1 up to 0.5 E*, 0.5 at E*, 0 at 1.5 E*; E* = ESP above which yields are seriously affected (FAO_SB39 Table 32: 55/35/10; 6 for extremely sensitive = assumed)
factor_assumptions.RY_pH: 1 for pH 5.5-8.4; -0.25 RY per pH unit above 8.4; -0.20 per unit below 5.5 (assumed; FAO_SB39 only states pH 8.2 as sodic diagnostic)
factor_assumptions.RY_SOC: 0.75 + 0.25 min(SOC/0.6 %, 1) (assumed: dryland soils are productive under fertigation at low SOC)
factor_assumptions.RY_coarse_fragments: 1 up to 15 vol %, linear to 0.5 at 55 %, to 0.2 at 80 % (assumed; FAO_SB55 lists stoniness as class-determining factor, limits not read)
factor_assumptions.RY_depth: clip((depth-20 cm)/(Zr_min-20 cm),0,1)^0.6 with Zr_min from FAO56 Table 22 (curve assumed); 0 below 20 cm
factor_assumptions.RY_slope: non-terraced: 1 up to 3 deg, 0.5 at 10 deg, 0 at 18 deg (assumed); terraced: 1 within the terrace limit (20-30 deg, assumed) and depth >= 40 cm
factor_assumptions.RY_water: 1 - Ky (1 - supply/demand), Ky = 1 (assumed; FAO-33 Ky not read)
factor_assumptions.classes: S1 >= 0.8, S2 0.6-0.8, S3 0.4-0.6, N < 0.4 relative yield (FAO_SB55: tops of S2 and S3 = 80 % / 60 %; 40 % bound assumed)

monte_carlo.note: outer = parameter draws, inner = input-noise draws; feasibility interval over outer draws

BATJES_2024.citation: Batjes, N.H., Calisto, L. & de Sousa, L.M. (2024). Providing quality-assessed and standardised soil data to support global mapping and modelling (WoSIS snapshot 2023). Earth Syst. Sci. Data 16:4735-4765.

FAO56.citation: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration - Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56.

FAO_IDP29.citation: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1.

FAO_SB39.citation: Abrol, I.P., Yadav, J.S.P. & Massoud, F.I. (1988). Salt-affected soils and their management. FAO Soils Bulletin 39.

FAO_SB55.citation: FAO (1985). Guidelines: Land evaluation for irrigated agriculture. FAO Soils Bulletin 55.

FAO_WH91.citation: Critchley, W. & Siegert, K. (1991). A manual for the design and construction of water harvesting schemes for plant production. FAO AGL/MISC/17/91.

GRAVUER_2019.citation: Gravuer, K., Gennet, S. & Throop, H.L. (2019). Organic amendment additions to rangelands: a meta-analysis of multiple ecosystem outcomes. Global Change Biology 25:1152-1170.

HASSANI_2020.citation: Hassani, A., Azapagic, A. & Shokri, N. (2020). Predicting long-term dynamics of soil salinity and sodicity on a global scale. PNAS 117(52):33017-33027.

MAAS_HOFFMAN_1977.citation: Maas, E.V. & Hoffman, G.J. (1977). Crop salt tolerance - current assessment. J. Irrigation and Drainage Div. ASCE 103(IR2):115-134.

SWATPLUS_K.citation: SWAT+ Input/Output documentation, 'Soil Erodibility Factor' (equations of Williams, J.R. 1995, EPIC).

limitations: No real restoration outcome data: agreement with rules measures consistency, not real-world success.
Water SOURCE availability, groundwater depth/quality, aquifer sustainability and treated-wastewater location are not mapped.
pH/SOC/texture/CF/depth are third-party ML maps with limited arid skill; SOC has no regional skill in the held-out region (R2~0).
Salinity/sodicity effective resolution ~1 km; climate/water ~4 km; do not read polygon values below that scale as measurements.
Wind erosion, flash floods, frost and market/economic factors are not modelled.
